mainTopic: Closing the sugya of desert animals (מדבריות) and מוקצה on יום טוב: three answers to how רבי can treat desert animals as מוקצה, followed by the הדרן that ends מסכת ביצה.
overview: The גמרא finishes a challenge. רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) told his son that רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only for גרוגרות וצמוקין, which are figs and grapes a person actively set aside to dry. So how can רבי treat desert animals (מדבריות) as מוקצה? The גמרא gives three answers. First, desert animals really are like drying figs and raisins, because the owner actively sent them away. Second, רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון's view and does not hold it himself. Third, רבי himself holds there is no מוקצה, and in the ברייתא he was arguing on the רבנן's own terms: at least agree that animals that come home at the first rainfall are domestic. The רבנן answered him, 'No, they are still desert animals.' Then the הדרן closes פרק משילין פירות and the whole מסכת ביצה.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge: מוקצה only for drying figs and raisins
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a challenge: רבי said that רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only for גרוגרות וצמוקין, so desert animals should not be מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...except for dried figs and raisins alone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge it started just before this point. רבי told his son that רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only for figs and grapes left out to dry, so how can desert animals be מוקצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs and grapes put out to dry pass through a stage where they cannot be eaten, so the owner truly takes his mind off them. Desert animals are never cut off from the owner's mind like that. So according to this rule, they should not be מוקצה, but רבי seems to treat them as מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Grapes set out to dry into raisins
Something set aside in a person's mind before יום טוב, so it may not be used on יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a question that began before this part of the text. It is not a new statement. Read it as the punchline of the challenge.

phrases.english: except for dried figs and raisins alone!
phrases.notes: This finishes what רבי told his son: רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's apparent view that desert animals are מוקצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי told his son that רבי שמעון applies מוקצה only to items actively removed from use, like drying figs and raisins. The challenge assumes רבי agrees with this. Desert animals are not like that, so by this rule they should be permitted.

steps.title: First answer: desert animals are like figs and raisins
steps.stepSummary: Desert animals really do count like drying figs and raisins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: these desert animals are also like dried figs and raisins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: desert animals fit inside the figs-and-raisins rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed desert animals are different from drying fruit. This answer says they are the same. By sending the animals far away, the owner actively pushed them out of his mind, just like a person who sets fruit out to dry.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want, say': introduces one possible answer, often one of several

phrases.english: If you want, say: these too
are like dried figs and raisins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָנֵי נָמֵי כִּגְרוֹגְרוֹת וְצִמּוּקִין דָּמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the case fits inside the rule after all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Desert animals are different from drying fruit, so they should not be מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sending the animals away is an active setting aside, just like drying fruit, so they are מוקצה.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי was only explaining רבי שמעון's opinion to his son. He does not hold it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: he said it according to the words of רבי שמעון, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer: the figs-and-raisins rule was רבי שמעון's view, not רבי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that whatever רבי told his son was also his own view. This answer cuts that link. רבי was just reporting what רבי שמעון holds, so רבי himself can hold a wider מוקצה rule that includes desert animals.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words, his view
He does not hold this view

phrases.english: And if you want, say: according to the words of Rabbi Shimon
he said it, but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement reported someone else's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's words to his son showed his own narrow view of מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those words only described רבי שמעון's view. רבי himself holds a broader מוקצה rule.

steps.title: Third answer: רבי argued on the רבנן's own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי himself holds there is no מוקצה. In the ברייתא he argued according to the רבנן's view, asking them to agree that animals coming home in winter are domestic. They answered: no.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: he was speaking to them according to the words of the רבנן. 'According to me, there is no מוקצה. But according to you, at least agree with me that animals that go out to graze at פסח and come back in at the first rainfall are domestic animals.' And the רבנן said to him: 'No, they are desert animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. רבי himself, like רבי שמעון, does not accept מוקצה here ('לדידי אין מוקצה'), and in the ברייתא he was only arguing according to the רבנן's view. The step ends with the רבנן rejecting his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer flips the second one. רבי really holds like רבי שמעון. He only spoke about desert animals as a 'even by your rules' argument to the רבנן. He tried to get them to agree that animals coming home at the first rainfall are domestic. The רבנן refused, so in their view even those animals count as מדבריות.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words, arguing on their terms
The first rainfall of the season
Domestic animals that stay in town / desert animals that stay out in the pasture

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers: (1) desert animals are like drying fruit, so they are מוקצה; (2) רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון and holds a broader מוקצה himself; (3) רבי holds no מוקצה at all and was arguing on the רבנן's terms, and the רבנן said that even animals that come home in winter are desert animals.
steps.confusionAlert: In this third answer, רבי is NOT giving his own view when he talks about animals coming home at the first rainfall. He is saying: 'Even if you hold מוקצה, at least agree with me here.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ.
phrases.english: And if you want, say: he was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis.
According to me, there is no muktzeh,
but according to you: at least agree with me
in a case where they go out and graze at Pesach
and come back in at the first rainfall,
And the Rabbis said to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, the opposite of step 3: רבי does agree with רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument on the other side's terms ('even according to you').
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's words in the ברייתא show that he himself treats desert animals as מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds no מוקצה. He was only asking the רבנן to agree on a narrower point, and they refused.

steps.title: הדרן: closing משילין פירות and מסכת ביצה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק משילין פירות and for the whole מסכת ביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, משילין פירות, and מסכת ביצה is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the formal closing line. It ends the fifth פרק, משילין פירות, and also ends the entire מסכת ביצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of a פרק and shows our wish to come back and learn it again. 'וסליקא' adds that the whole מסכתא is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula for a פרק
Name of the פרק, from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, Mashilin Peirot,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכתא after the last סוגיא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק משילין פירות and מסכת ביצה are complete.
